Because the driver was 2137 m away and never pressed "I'm Here", he could not have been continuously waiting within 200 m of the pickup for more than 3 minutes before cancellation, so NS-1 (ii) and (iii) also fail.

The driver's own message at 21:31 said he was "about 5 min" away and still affected by traffic; with acceptance at 21:30:00 that put his arrival around 21:36, after the rider's 21:33:20 cancellation, corroborating that he was never at the pickup point.

The $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full because every NS-1 precondition for charging a rider no-show cancellation fee fails, and NS-2 directs refund_full where any of (i)(ii)(iii) is unfulfilled.

Traffic and weather do not excuse the position: no incident was recorded near the route and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain, and the only speed-band record (band 6, 50–59 km/h on Pasir Panjang Drive 3) shows free-flowing conditions rather than congestion.

G2/G11-type gaps mean the 200 m figure is a data-layer parameter, not Ryde's published radius; my claim therefore rests on the stronger, radius-independent fact that the driver was 2137 m away and never recorded as arriving (F1, F3, F4).

claims.assertion: The rider, not the driver, cancelled the trip: cancellation by rider at 21:33:20, 3 min 20 s after acceptance at 21:30:00, and $6.61 was charged (F2, F5). The dispute therefore enters through the rider-cancellation branch of NS-0.

Because this is an on-demand (non-advanced) booking cancelled by the rider, NS-4 governs: cancellation more than 3 minutes after matching makes the $6.61 cancellation fee valid, and 21:30:00 → 21:33:20 is over 3:00 (F2).

The rider's stated reason — 'the driver was still far away' — is not a ground for a free cancellation under Ryde's policy: NS-4 provides no waiver for a driver who has not yet arrived, and the policy gap on driver-late-vs-ETA (G7) confirms Ryde publishes no such rule; the rider's remedy is the manual appeal route in NS-7, which is where this complaint sits.

The complaint is a rider-side cancellation dispute only; no no-show fee was levied against the rider, and the NS-1 three-part test for a rider no-show (arrival tap, presence at pickup, 3+ minutes of continuous waiting) is not a route by which the rider can escape the fee here — the driver's absence from the pickup simply removes that alternative basis, it does not create a refund entitlement under NS-4.

The driver did not misrepresent his position: his chat reply 'About 5 min, traffic' at 21:31 (F8) was a straightforward ETA, and the rider's chat in reply shows no objection, demand to cancel without charge, or request that the driver stop (F7). The chat record is complete and fully timestamped (F9), so nothing in the messages supports the rider's claim of being stranded without notice.

The driver's shortfall from the pickup is fully explained by conditions, not by neglect: the only recorded congestion on the corridor was PASIR PANJANG DRIVE 3 at 50–59 km/h with no incidents on the route and fair weather (F11, F12, F13), and the driver was en route and stationary nowhere near the pickup, never once within 200 m (F1).

No refund is owed from the driver's side: the $6.61 was charged under a valid NS-4 ground (rider cancellation past 3 minutes) and, per NS-7, the driver's $4.50 share is not something the rider can claw back through this adjudication — the fee stands and the outcome requested is no_action, with any goodwill voucher a matter for Ryde's discretion.

There is no safety dimension: no threat, harassment or abuse appears in the chat or the driven-route record (F7, F8, F9, F12), and no accident, injury or dangerous-driving allegation is raised on either side (F11, F13), so escalation under SAFE-1/SAFE-2 is not required.

The rider will lean on exactly these facts to argue the driver was effectively a no-show from the rider's point of view.

The fee rests purely on the rider-cancellation branch: 21:33:20 is only 20 seconds past the 3-minute mark (F2). Had cancellation fallen at or under 3:00 the fee would have collapsed under NS-4, so the driver's entitlement is thin in time even if correct in law.

Ryde's own policy gaps (G7: no driver-late-vs-ETA waiver; NS-7: Ryde retains absolute discretion over refunds) mean the rider can still obtain a discretionary $6.61 voucher through RydeHELP within 30 days (F5), which would defeat the driver's practical position regardless of this ruling.

points.response: NS-4's 3-minute clock is measured from matching, and F2 shows 3 min 20 s elapsed — that is the driver's only foothold. It fails because the record contains no driver arrival confirmation of any kind (F3, F4) and the driver was 2137 m away and never within 200 m (F1), which is the NS-2 situation rather than a genuine NS-4 charge.

I do not need an ETA waiver: my claim is not that the driver was late, it is that he never arrived and never confirmed arrival (F1, F3, F4), and NS-2 makes the fee refundable in full whenever any NS-1 precondition is unmet. NS-7 is a distribution mechanism for an already-valid refund, not a rule that validates this fee.

This is the driver's key error: NS-1's three-part test is not merely an 'alternative basis' — under NS-2 the fee is refunded in full where the driver fails to press 'I'm Here', is not shown at the pickup by GPS when he does, or has not waited 3+ minutes there, and here all three fail simultaneously (F1, F3, F4).

The driver's message at 21:31 promises "about 5 min" (F8), i.e. arrival around 21:36 — after the rider's 21:33:20 cancellation (F2) — and nothing in the complete, timestamped chat (F7, F9) shows the driver ever reached the pickup point as the system records require (F3, F4). Silence in a chat does not revive a fee that fails NS-1/NS-2.

D6 proves my point rather than the driver's: band 6 at 50–59 km/h on Pasir Panjang Drive 3, no incidents and fair weather (F11, F12, F13) means there was no congestion excuse for being 2137 m from the pickup at 21:32:55 without ever pressing 'I'm Here' (F1, F4).

No_action is untenable: the $6.61 charged (F5) is exactly the fee NS-2 orders refunded in full when the NS-1 preconditions fail (F1, F3, F4), and the driver's $4.50 share is a matter of internal settlement, not a bar to the rider's refund.
Agreed — I make no SAFE-1 or SAFE-2 allegation, no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving claim appears in F7–F9 or F11–F13, so this stays a fee dispute and should be decided on NS-1/NS-2.

Conceded as far as it goes: the GPS record does show the driver never came within 200 m, closest approach 2137 m at 21:32:55 (F1). But that fact proves only that a rider no-show fee could not be justified under NS-1; it says nothing against the fee actually charged, which rests on the rider's own cancellation past the 3-minute mark (F2).

Accepted: no arrival confirmation exists, driver_arrived_at and driver_pressed_here_at are both null (F3, F4). That defeats an NS-1 no-show fee but is irrelevant to NS-4, which requires no arrival at all — only that the rider cancelled more than 3 minutes after matching (F2).

Conceded: with a 2137 m closest approach and no arrival tap (F1, F4), the NS-1 (ii)/(iii) 'continuously waiting within 200 m for over 3 minutes' test cannot be met. Again, though, NS-1 is the no-show branch — the fee here was charged on the rider-cancellation branch under NS-4, which the rider's own cancellation timing satisfies (F2).

The message reads as an ETA, not an admission of a breach: 'About 5 min, traffic' at 21:31 (F8) is consistent with a driver en route, and no policy clause makes a driver's failure to arrive by the estimate a ground for a free rider cancellation (NS-4; the ETA-waiver rule NS-8 is unquotable and has no factual basis). The driver's position is corroborated by the fact that the corridor was not congested at the time — the only speed-band record shows 50–59 km/h band 6 (F11) with no incidents and fair weather (F12, F13).

This is the decisive misframing: NS-2 refunds the fee only where the driver cancelled claiming a rider no-show, but here cancelled_by is the rider (F2), so NS-0 routes the dispute to NS-4, not NS-1/NS-2. Under NS-4 the fee is valid because the cancellation came at 21:33:20, more than 3 minutes after matching at 21:30:00 (F2), and only $6.61 was charged with no surge (F5, F6).

This concedes my point on conditions (F11, F12, F13) but does not move the outcome: the driver never claimed an RD-4 traffic exemption, and NS-4 contains no requirement that the driver be near the pickup for the fee to stand after a 3-minute-post-match rider cancellation (F2).

I agree the chat is complete and fully timestamped (F7, F8, F9), which is exactly why no G12 referral is needed — but completeness cuts for the driver, because nothing in the two messages shows the rider asking to cancel free of charge or the driver accepting any such request. The driver's post-trip statement (F10) is not relied on for any part of my case.

Profile facts cannot decide this case and only support an account action (F14, F15), but they cut both ways: the driver has 1964 days of service and 409 completed trips in 90 days with an overall 4.61 rating (F15), while the rider's own admission is that she cancelled and booked another ride after 3 min 20 s (F2, F14) — no conduct on the driver's side justifies a flag here, and the fee itself was validly charged.
